messages:
alex_w: Quick question — noticed a couple weird behaviors around generation params (stop sequences + tiny max_tokens, temp/top_p combos, and logprobs). Are we aligned on the contract?

maya: can you paste the request + what you saw?

alex_w: sure — repro below (simplified):
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-v1-base",
  "prompt": "Q: Translate to fr:\nHello\nA:",
  "max_tokens": 2,
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 0.8,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```
What I observed: API returned 3 tokens in the "text" and logprobs was null. Also when temperature=0 I expected deterministic greedy and top_p to be ignored, but behavior seemed inconsistent across runtimes.

jin: short answers from contract side:
- max_tokens must be a hard cap on generated tokens (not counting prompt). We should never return more than max_tokens.
- stop sequences are post-processing truncation; they can produce fewer tokens but never cause > max_tokens.
- temperature==0 should imply greedy decoding and top_p ignored. We should explicitly document that.

samir: agree on those, + add: if stop sequence is detected mid-token (byte-level) we need deterministic handling — either return partial token or ensure tokenization boundaries. Current runtime bug may be counting bytes after stop removal which can lead to off-by-one.

maya: action items: alex, can you open a PR with a unit test that covers:
- max_tokens=1 + stop that would trigger immediately
- temp=0 + top_p!=1 -> ensure top_p ignored and output deterministic
- request logprobs=5 + streaming vs non-streaming path (logprobs should be present or explicit null with reason)

alex_w: yes. I'll put tests in runtime/generation/tests and add a contract note in docs/api/generate.md. Example expected response I will assert against:
```json
{
  "id": "gen_abc",
  "object": "generation",
  "choices": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "text": "Bonjour",
      "logprobs": {
        "tokens": ["Bonjour"],
        "token_logprobs": [-0.2],
        "top_logprobs": [{"Bonjour": -0.2}]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Notes: always include the "logprobs" field in the choice object — if unavailable, set to `null` and include a top-level `warnings` array explaining why (e.g., "logprobs unavailable for streaming responses").

jin: +1 to always include the field. Backcompat: existing clients may expect missing field vs null — we should mention this in CHANGELOG and roll it out as deprecation (emit both "logprobs": null and a compatibility header for one release).

samir: regarding temp/top_p: implementation detail is sampling pipeline uses temperature scaling on logits then nucleus sampling for top_p. But if temp==0 we short-circuit to argmax. Document that order. Also test interplay with top_k.

alex_w: one more weirdness: when stop triggers we sometimes return trailing whitespace/newline, which breaks some downstream postprocessors that assert exact truncation. I'll add a test vector: prompt ends with partial sentence and stop=["\n\n"], expected returned text must not include the stop tokens and trailing whitespace trimmed.

maya: good. For the PR include: test vectors, docs change, CHANGLEOG entry, and a small migration note for SDKs. @jin can you review the sampling spec?

jin: will do. ping me when PR is up.

alex_w: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1423 (wip). Added tests for max_tokens+stop and temp=0 behavior. Need a quick runtime review.

ci-bot: ci/cd started for PR #1423 — tests running.

maya: thanks. once CI passes we'll merge into canary and run internal smoke with a subset of customers. I'll coordinate rollout schedule in #eng-releases. :calendar:

samir: FYI, I'll add a small fuzz test to catch tokenization edgecases that could make stop detection ambiguous.

alex_w: nice. TL;DR: contract decisions: max_tokens hard cap, stop removes tokens post-hoc (no overrun), temp=0 -> greedy (ignore top_p/top_k), always include logprobs field (null if unavailable) + warnings header. I'll summarize in the PR description.

maya: perfect — thanks team.

alex_w: tagging folks who asked: @maya @jin @samir. We'll follow-up on any regressions after canary rollout. :thumbsup:
